text:
Nadia: Heads-up  I just opened a PR that restructures the optkit examples into a language-aware layout (examples/en, examples/es). It also renames a few quant profile files for clarity. PR #5128
Owen: Interesting. Are we shipping translated content now?
Nadia: Not full translations, just scaffolding for localized example variants and a single Spanish translation of the shortseq batching README as a pilot. The issue is many SDK snippets still point to the old flat paths so staging linkcheck flags ~10 broken links.
Tyler: Can you paste the failing paths?
Nadia: From the preview log: 
- /optimize/examples/batching/shortseq.md -> moved to /optkit/examples/en/batching/shortseq.md
- /optimize/quant_profiles/shortseq_default.md -> renamed to /optkit/quant-profiles/shortseq/default.md
- src/snippets/python/shortseq_usage.py -> imports example via relative path that no longer exists
- docs/locales/es/shortseq_readme.md -> new file (not linked yet) but we want a canonical pointer from the English page

Marina: I like the locale folders but we need a canonical link strategy so external teams don't link into language-specific URLs. Suggest we keep canonical at /optkit/examples/batching/shortseq and redirect to /optkit/examples/en/batching/shortseq for now.
Owen: Agree. We should add a small frontmatter key canonical: /optkit/examples/batching/shortseq to the localized files and update the build to emit Link: rel=canonical headers for the HTML build.
Tyler: For the snippet imports, easiest is to add a docs preprocessor that rewrites snippet paths during build and a one-line comment in the snippet to show the new canonical path. That way we avoid immediate churn in other repos.
Nadia: Proposed quick fixes:
- Add docs/_data/legacy_paths.yml with old->canonical mapping
- Add a Sphinx transform docs/_ext/canonical_redirect.py to read the mapping and create redirect pages and canonical headers
- Run a sed/patch on src/snippets to update imports and append a migration comment pointing to the canonical path
- Add a lightweight snippet smoke test to docs-ci that imports python snippets and lints JS snippets

Marina: Also, for the Spanish pilot, please add x-translated: true in frontmatter to help docs search and filter. We'll iterate on translations later.
Owen: I can own the Sphinx transform and canonical header. I'll add an opt-in env var so CI can test both behaviours.
Tyler: I'll prepare the sed patch for snippets and a small pytest that runs the example module import and ensures no ModuleNotFoundError. I'll also add a test that the snippet includes a comment like "MIGRATION: canonical -> /optkit/examples/batching/shortseq" so we can track updates.
Nadia: Posting a grep in ~10m with all files referencing old paths. Also, can we be careful with anchors? Some product pages link to /optimize/quant_profiles/shortseq_default#fp16. If we canonicalize without preserving anchors we'll break those.
Owen: Two approaches: 1) in the redirect page, add client-side JS that maps legacy fragments to the new fragments, or 2) emit legacy anchor aliases as meta tags on the canonical page. I prefer (1) for speed. I'll add a small anchors.json that maps old tokens to new tokens and a tiny script to handle fallback.#
Tyler: One implementation detail: our snippet bundler currently treats top-level comments as metadata. Appending migration comments might require updating the bundler to ignore them. I'll include a bundler update in the PR so the comment doesn't appear in rendered code blocks.
Marina: Plan and owners:
- Owen: canonical redirect transform + anchors.json + client fallback script (PR today)
- Tyler: snippet sed patches + snippet import smoke tests + bundler tweak (PR today)
- Nadia: grep + update PR description, add staging preview link and list of broken links (follow-up here)
- Marina: add frontmatter keys and coordinate with search team for translated pilot indexing (will send a short doc)

docs-bot: Staging preview: https://staging-docs.redwood.ai/optkit/preview/5128 (10 link errors) :mag_right:

Tyler: I'll take 6 of the link errors (snippets and imports). Owen: you take 3 (redirects/anchors). Nadia: you'll own the new translated file linkage and canonical pointers.
Nadia: Yes. Also note: one external repo references the old quant profile path in a cookbook; I'll open a quick PR in that repo after our redirects are live. We'll delay deleting old paths until after partners are updated.
Owen: Adding a small telemetry event to redirects (non-sensitive) so we can see how many hits the legacy URLs still get in the two-week window. Useful to decide deletion timing.
Marina: One small UX ask: update the docs Console link in the SDK examples to point to the canonical page rather than language-specific pages. That will reduce cross-team confusion.
Tyler: Noted. I'll include that in the snippets patch.
Nadia: Thanks everyone. I'll drop the grep output here in 10m and tag the PRs. If anything blocks, ping me directly. :thumbsup:
